changes: Replace Object.values/map/rest partition-spec lists with one streaming scan of own window definitions.
Preserve global/mixed/incompatible topology precedence and skip further key comparisons once the result is known.
Add optional scoped topology planning with admitted stable-key comparison workspace, detached partition expressions and transactional result ownership.
Release each comparison workspace immediately and preserve parent/sibling ownership on failure.

coverage: Equivalent 2-window and 1000-window plans use the same reserved peak; exact peak succeeds and one byte less rejects.
Binary partition literal and input-list mutation cannot alter a scoped returned plan.
Failed planning leaves a preexisting sibling allocation intact.
Mixed global/partitioned reason retains precedence after an earlier partition mismatch.
Existing query/window/task and HTTP fixtures remain green.

remaining: Task discovery still returns plain TaskInput arrays; scoped topology integration is a prerequisite for completing owned task discovery, not completion of that larger contract.
Unscoped callers preserve borrowed partition-expression behavior; only explicitly scoped results own detached expressions.
Task ranges, path/partition metadata, callback outputs and internal window-task plan lifetimes still require ownership integration.
No wall-clock speedup or whole-runtime heap cap is claimed from the workspace test.
